fun_highlights: The calling system (soldier/scholar/maker/wanderer) genuinely differentiates lives structurally — a soldier's arc has distinct moments (m_soldier_ghost, vx_soldier_war, e_soldier_old) that a scholar never sees, so picking up the phone and finding a soldier life actually reads differently from a scholar one.

Era cards (war/plague/plenty/hard/turning) are a good macro-layer: being born into a war year produces a texturally different childhood opening and gates specific cards (w_war_call, w_war_loss, vx_soldier_war) that stay invisible in settled years. For a snacker who plays in short bursts, the era announcement on birth is a quick orientation signal that this run will be distinct.

Callback cards are the game's best feature for the mobile_snacker: they close arcs from 20-40 years prior with precise prose that references the original choice. cb_books_late, cb_lookaway, cb_strayed, cb_home_keep all land with a satisfying click of recognition. In a 5-minute session these are the 'wow' moments.

The dynasty layer provides a real cross-session pull for short-session players: the motto crystallising mid-session (The family's character has settled into words: 'Beauty is the only argument we trust'), the house rising a seat, heirlooms accumulating — these are legible one-sentence milestones that make each pickup feel like forward motion.

Prose variety within cards is genuinely high. The marriage lines alone have 8 variants, child-birth lines have 8+ with a separate late-birth pool. freshPick() with session-level deduplication means within a single sitting the same line rarely repeats, which is the most important thing for a snacker reading on a phone.
The constellation / star-map and the chronicle make a session feel substantial even if it was only 4 choices — there is an artefact, not just a score.
staleness: The structural template is rigid and becomes visible by dynasty 4-5. Every life follows: childhood card (c_origin always fires 3-5) → y_calling (14-22) → y_love1 or a_meet_late → a_marry → a_child → a_work or midlife fillers → m_health or m_parent_age → elder cap → die. Even with different vocation arcs layered on top, the skeleton is the same. By dynasty 8 (House Holloway, Esme) and dynasty 11 (Iris Bjornsen) the transcript shows the same scaffolding re-emerging with only the vocation arc and a handful of trait/era cards changing the flavour.

107 of 144 cards are once-per-life, and 25 are once-per-dynasty. That means the repeatable pool servicing the adult/midlife band (ages 28-64, roughly half a life) is only about 37 cards — and several of those have 14-18 year cooldowns. The transcripts show the thin patch plainly: adult lives in dynasties 4-10 repeatedly draw a_work, a_neighbour, a_small_lie, a_fallow, m_who_became in nearly the same order. The mid-life years feel like filler between the structural pillars.

The love/marry/child sequence fires in virtually every coupled life, and the engine's own nudges (30% push on y_love1 each draw, 55-62% push on a_marry once in love, 33% push on a_child once married) make it near-certain. Out of 30+ lives in the transcript only a handful are genuinely solitary. For the mobile_snacker who has played 6-7 dynasties, the domestic arc is already a known quantity — the interest is in which vocation arc sits on top of it, not the arc itself.

The once-per-dynasty gate on 25 cards, while well-intentioned, creates a specific staleness pattern for long-running dynasties: by generation 3-4 the best structural variety cards (s_from_nothing, d_ancestor, d_motto_test, cb_books_late, e_craft, e_journey, e_peace, m_peer_dies) have been burned and cannot return. Dynasty 6 (House Quint, 5 gens) and Dynasty 12 (House Thorne) show noticeably thinner cards in later generations — later heirs draw more generic filler (a_fallow, m_smaller_body, a_recognition) because the interesting once-per-dynasty beats are exhausted.

The c_origin opener fires every life at age 3-5. Despite its 8-variant text, the mobile reader encounters it as the first card every single life. After 10+ lives this pattern is conditioned — 'oh, the origin card again' — even when the text variant is different. The opener loses its freshness as an event and becomes infrastructure.

Surnames and given names are drawn from small pools (30 each, 30 surnames). In the transcripts within 15 dynasties: 'Cleo' appears as a given name in Dynasty 3, 4, 9, 10, and 12; 'Otto' in Dynasty 4, 6, 9, 10, 12; 'Emory' in Dynasty 10, 11, 12. For a snacker reading the chronicle, repeated names across unrelated dynasties dilute the sense that each house is its own story.

The observation system (ambient prose from observe()) fires on stat thresholds and is not gated on once-per-life. The transcripts show lines like 'Books have become a country she can live in' and 'He has kept, against most of the evidence, a stubborn appetite for the days' repeating across multiple lives in a single session. These are background texture, but after several sessions the same lines become wallpaper.

improvements.what: Add 15-20 mid-adult/midlife repeatable cards with longer cooldowns (20-22 years) focused on the work/craft/relationship maintenance band (ages 32-58). These do not need to be structurally significant — short, 2-choice moments that vary the filler years. The current filler cards (a_fallow, a_neighbour, a_small_lie, m_smaller_body, a_recognition) are good but too few for how much time a life spends in that band.
improvements.why: 107/144 cards are once-per-life. The repeatable pool for the longest band of a life (mid-adult to midlife, ~30 years) is thin enough that a long-session player on dynasty 5+ will see the same 4-5 cards cycling. This is the most immediately fixable staleness.

improvements.what: Increase the given-name and surname pools — double them. Given names: 60 each gender. Surnames: 60. The current 30/30/30 pools produce name collisions across dynasties by session 8-10.
improvements.why: For a snacker reading the chronicle after a session, seeing 'Cleo' as founder of Dynasty 3, heir of Dynasty 4, heir of Dynasty 9, and two others breaks the immersion that each house is a unique lineage. Name collisions are the cheapest form of staleness to fix.

improvements.what: Add a second 'opener' variant that can fire instead of c_origin on second+ playthroughs: a card that positions the heir specifically within the house's existing reputation/era/seat rather than restating early childhood generically. Gate it on gen>=2 and randomise which opener fires (50/50).
improvements.why: c_origin fires every life at age 3-5 with no dynasty-awareness. After 10 lives the player knows this card is coming before they can walk. A second opener that starts from 'born into a house known for X' would make the opening feel different between sessions.

improvements.what: Promote 5-8 of the best once-per-dynasty cards (d_ancestor, d_motto_test, e_craft, e_journey, e_peace, m_peer_dies) to a soft-repeat system: eligible again after 3 generations, with different text variants, rather than burned forever. Flag the variant so the prose acknowledges it is a recurring pattern ('Again the question comes, as it did to [ancestor].') rather than pretending it's novel.
improvements.why: Long dynasties (gens 4-6) are penalised by card exhaustion — the most interesting structural beats are all burned. The fix should acknowledge recurrence rather than hide it.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 cross-dynasty callbacks that reference a specific ancestor by name and epitaph: 'Your grandmother [name] — [epitaph] — left a question no one in the family has answered.' These should fire once per dynasty and produce a choice that either continues, reverses, or ignores the ancestor's theme. Currently d_ancestor references lineage narratively but not directly enough to feel personal.
improvements.why: The dynasty layer's strongest pull for a snacker is the accumulation of specific named ancestors. A callback that uses a stored epitaph verbatim would make the lineage feel like a real through-line rather than a reputation meter.

verdict: A Life is a beautifully written generational sim with real structural variety in its vocation and era systems, but by dynasty 5 the life-template (origin → calling → love → marry → child → midlife fillers → elder cap) is clearly visible through the prose, and the thin repeatable card pool for the 32-58 age band means most of a life is filler between the memorable once-only beats — genuinely fun for 3-4 dynasties, stale before 8.
